core.title: Declare journeys as topology above flow routers: entrypoint, continuations, explicit terminals
core.given: A journey document composing routing decisions across flow routers, each flow router selecting exactly one linear user/system flow
core.when: the planner authors or changes the journey's entrypoint, routes, continuations or terminals
core.then: Declare the journey as {station-entrypoint, entrypoint-interlocking, route-continuations, explicit-terminals}: if exposed, its starting actions on the consumer-facing start surface (stack name via profile: idiom.routing#journey_start_surface), its consumer surfaces and first flow router; and for every route, after its selected user/system flow completes, either an explicit terminal or a continuation from (flow_router_id, route_id) via a named artifact that user/system flow produces to the next flow router.
prefer: Compose flow router -> user/system flow -> flow router; keep each flow router a local boundary selecting one linear user/system flow.

Ownership: the flow router selects the user/system flow, the user/system flow executor (stack component via profile: roles.runtime_components#user_system_flow_executor) executes product capabilities linearly, the journey owns continuation.

Exposed journeys: the stack binds the declared start-surface actions (profile: idiom.routing#journey_start_surface) to the journey entry through its entry-binding idiom (profile: idiom.routing#journey_entry_binding).
Treat journey artifacts as planner data; a separate runtime may introduce a journey executor (stack component via profile: roles.runtime_components#journey_executor).
avoid: Recursive flow routers (one selecting or invoking another).

Moving product capability execution out of the user/system flow executor (stack component via profile: roles.runtime_components#user_system_flow_executor), or letting any of the three absorb the others.
Implicitly dangling routes, or continuations not keyed by an artifact the selected user/system flow produces.
Encoding runtime execution (e.g. a journey executor, profile: roles.runtime_components#journey_executor) into the semantic journey definition.
core.why: Keeping continuation in the journey lets routing compose across flow routers without recursive flow routers or split product capability execution, so each boundary stays local and verifiable.
evidence: The journey document validates against the stack's canonical journey schema (profile: layout.schemas#journey_schema).
Exposed journeys list start-surface actions (stack name via profile: idiom.routing#journey_start_surface) / consumer surfaces and an entrypoint flow router.

Every (flow_router_id, route_id) reached by the journey has either an explicit terminal or a continuation naming an artifact produced by that route's selected user/system flow and a target flow router.
No flow router selects another flow router; product capability execution remains in the user/system flow executor (stack component via profile: roles.runtime_components#user_system_flow_executor).
verification: Journey shape check: journey -> {station-entrypoint, entrypoint-interlocking, route-continuations, explicit-terminals}; journey documents are validated against the stack's canonical journey schema (profile: layout.schemas#journey_schema).
continuation = binding from one (flow_router_id, route_id) pair, through an artifact produced by that route's selected user/system flow, to the next flow router.
terminal = explicit declaration that a route ends the journey rather than continuing to another flow router.

station_entrypoint: exposed journeys declare start-surface actions (stack name via profile: idiom.routing#journey_start_surface) and consumer surfaces; the stack binds those actions to the journey entry through its entry-binding idiom (profile: idiom.routing#journey_entry_binding); the concrete stack rule that performs the binding is realization detail and stays with the realization.

values: journey document (the plan-artifact kind validated against the stack's canonical journey schema, profile: layout.schemas#journey_schema)
consumer start surface (stack name via profile: idiom.routing#journey_start_surface)
flow router selects/invokes another flow router
product capability execution placed outside the user/system flow executor (stack component via profile: roles.runtime_components#user_system_flow_executor)

fires: Planner adds a new journey that should be startable from actions on the consumer-facing start surface (profile: idiom.routing#journey_start_surface).
Planner adds a route to a flow router used by a journey and must decide whether the route terminates or continues.
Planner wants control to pass to another flow router after a selected user/system flow finishes producing an artifact.
A plan proposes making a flow router select another flow router, or making a journey run product capabilities directly.
doesNotFire: Planner edits only a single flow router's user/system flow selection without touching any journey continuation or terminal.
Planner edits only product capability order inside one linear user/system flow.
Work on a journey-executor runtime implementation (stack component via profile: roles.runtime_components#journey_executor; governed by runtime conventions, not this semantic definition).

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kinds that play the plan-artifact role; the core needs the kind that is the journey document, so activation and checks can recognize it.
Location of the stack's canonical journey schema against which journey documents are validated (activation file-kind, evidence and the shape check defer to it).

The stack's concrete name for the consumer-facing start surface whose actions start an exposed journey; used by the entrypoint declaration in then, prefer[2], evidence, the station_entrypoint check and the activation task terms.

The stack's component that executes a selected user/system flow's product capabilities linearly; used by the ownership statements (prefer[1], avoid[1]), evidence[3] and the ownership-boundary finding in activation.

The stack's runtime component that may execute a journey, deliberately separate from the semantic journey definition; used by prefer[3], the avoid[3] example and the runtime-work exclusion in activation.
How the stack binds each declared start-surface action to the journey entry (the concrete binding target and shape); used by prefer[2] and the station_entrypoint check.
profileRequirements.bunValue: binds the declared journey router actions to {journeyId, path}

bunOnly.reason: References the Bun coder rule that realizes the entry binding; a concrete stack's rule id is realization detail. The binding shape {journeyId, path} itself is profile data (idiom.routing#journey_entry_binding), and the start surface name is profile data (idiom.routing#journey_start_surface).
Names the ATDD-Bun runtime realization; the core says only 'a separate runtime', and the executor component name comes from roles.runtime_components#journey_executor.

bunOnly.text: Bun binds those actions via coder.bun.journey-router-journey-routing
bunOnly.reason: Same split as prefer[2]: the stack qualifier and the Bun coder-rule reference are realization details with no stack-neutral equivalent; the surface name and the {journeyId, path} binding shape are carried by idiom.routing#journey_start_surface and idiom.routing#journey_entry_binding.

neutralityNotes: The planner-topology vocabulary (journey, flow router, user/system flow, product capability, route, continuation, terminal, entrypoint) is treated as stack-neutral ATDD planning vocabulary, since the profile vocabulary itself recognizes user/system flow, product capability and journey artifacts. The stack-specific component and surface names are reusable stack-idiom values, not obligations exclusive to one realization: 'journey router' (idiom.routing#journey_start_surface), 'FlowRunner' (roles.runtime_components#user_system_flow_executor), 'JourneyRunner' (roles.runtime_components#journey_executor) and the {journeyId, path} entry-binding shape (idiom.routing#journey_entry_binding) are carried as proposed profile keys and referenced consistently in the core obligation, activation facts/fires/exclusions and the verification entries; the closed vocabulary had no fitting keys, so all are proposed. What could not be made neutral: (1) the reference to the coder rule coder.bun.journey-router-journey-routing, a concrete stack's rule id that realizes the entry binding (stays with the realization, per notProfileKeys; the core verification describes the check generically and without naming the stack); (2) the 'Bun runtime' qualifier in prefer[3], which names the reference realization (core says only 'a separate runtime'); (3) the canonical journey schema path is data, not rule text, carried by the proposed layout.schemas#journey_schema key.
